text: Daniel José Santomé Lemus, born on 31 October 1993 in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, is a Spanish YouTuber known as Dalas Review or simply Dalas, who has 11 million subscribers on his main channel. He is the son of Juan Jose Santomé and Maria Sabrina Lemus Carmenatty and began using computers at age three, later developing an interest in 3D modelling and photo editing between ages 11 and 12. He enrolled in a multimedia degree but dropped out. Dalas started creating content in 2005 by adding nonsensical subtitles to film trailers, with "Dalas" derived from the first two letters of his first name, the first letter of his second last name, and the first two letters of his first last name in reverse. His career began in 2010 with the channel DTeamVlogs, gaining virality through a video titled "La niña believer" criticizing Justin Bieber's fans, and he launched his main channel, Dalas Review, in 2012. In July 2017, he won the Tolete Award for his parody of the Canarian accent in the video "Imitating 15 accents of Spain and Latin America (Very Bad)". In January 2021, he created a Pornhub account to upload videos on sexual education. He authored two novels: Fugitives in Time (2016), a science fiction work based on time travel that sold 16,000 units in four editions and was signed in Málaga, and The Ink. Beyond the Magic (2017), a story about Sveia, a young woman struggling with family and social issues who discovers a magical world. During the launch of the latter, he announced that instead of traditional book signings, he would host events featuring readings. In August 2021, he released the beta version of Stardeos, a video platform he developed over nine months, aiming to be a "fairer" version of YouTube where creators receive more visibility and content freedom, with no channel deletions or demonetization without a judge's order. The site faced technical issues, going offline during the first four hours due to over 150,000 users per minute, and servers could not handle the load; it returned online in October 2021, while Wrixy, a literary site, went offline due to unpaid maintenance costs. In October 2021, he uploaded a video criticizing 200 project workers and companies he contacted. In March 2022, he uploaded a video aggressively targeting Twitter haters, claiming to upload similar content for paid subscribers, and in June 2022, released a paid Stardeos video accusing AriGameplays of being unfaithful to JuanSGuarnizo with TheGrefg. He developed Fur Fun, a 3D adventure and platform game released on Steam on 10 February 2017, co-developed with Doky using Unreal Engine 4, which originated from a Kickstarter campaign titled "Kewpie - Jazzy" aiming to raise 92,000 euros but only securing 650 euros; the project was later renamed "Fur Fun" and launched on 8 December 2016. After its Steam release, it received negative reviews and was removed in January 2018. Between 2020 and 2021, he sought programmers to develop Fur Fun 2. On 23 December 2021, Dalas claimed to have received 10 million euros in Bitcoin from an anonymous individual via TorChat, allegedly to fund a laboratory focused on biological immortality research. He later investigated the source and found the donor was from Sinaloa, Mexico, and shifted his plans to use machine learning AI instead of human researchers. His relationship with María Rubio Sánchez (Miare) ended in March 2016, and Naya Chimlova uploaded a video explaining the breakup (now unavailable). In April 2016, Dalas responded to Miare's accusations of being a stalker in a video titled "estoy harto de mentiras y por eso hago este vídeo". In August 2016, Interviú published a headline "No sirves para nada, eres una puta" based on a complaint Miare filed in a Barcelona court. After Miare asked for his greyhound Argos, which he adopted in 2015, Dalas sued her to recover it in June 2016, winning the case in July 2017, with Miare sentenced to return the dog. Miare uploaded a half-hour video explaining her disagreement with the ruling and showed WhatsApp conversations allegedly showing Dalas mistreating the dog, which he denied in a video titled "tenía otro vídeo preparado, pero este mal rollo nunca acabará". In July 2017, several users uploaded videos alleging misconduct with Dalas. On 28 December 2018, Dalas, Lizy P, and two friends confronted Miare's parents in Barcelona's Sant Joan Despí neighborhood, where Miare's father hit Lizy and her mother bit a friend, leading to Lizy being hospitalized. In August 2019, Dalas sued Miare for false complaint. According to Miare's version, she lost Argos and her family adopted a twin named Marlos, and Dalas filed a complaint for misappropriation, claiming the dog was Argos. On 3 February 2021, the misappropriation complaint was archived after an expert concluded the dog was not Argos. Dalas uploaded a 56-minute video asserting the expert had been convinced to deny the dog was Argos, while Miare tweeted about the complaint. On 27 April 2021, he released a video showing the veterinarian retracted his earlier statement and confirmed the dog was Argos. On 18 May 2023, Dalas was sentenced to pay compensation to Miare's father for insults on his YouTube channel, and the same day, a judge ordered Miare and her parents to return the dog and pay compensation, citing document falsification and misappropriation, as they were found to still possess Argos and there was no twin. In January 2025, the Supreme Court sentenced Dalas to pay €12,000 in compensation for insults to Miare, cover appeal costs, and delete all videos that slandered Miare's father. On 4 October 2017, Wismichu uploaded a video titled "Así es Dalas Review" with 20.4 million views by February 2024, criticizing Dalas, calling him "miserable", "psychopath", "hyena", "bad person", "wretch", and "bastard", and insinuating he fled to Ireland to escape Spanish law. After this video, Dalas lost 310,000 subscribers, dropping from 5,700,000 to 5,390,000, temporarily hiding his subscriber count. On 5 October, he padlocked his Twitter account, which reopened on 6 October, and his YouTube channel was deleted due to mass reports but was reinstated hours later. In March 2018, he had an interview with Los Replicantes discussing court documents to refute accusations. On 18 May 2018, he released "se acabó, wismichu e ingrid" ("it's over, wismichu and ingrid"), an hour and forty-minute video refuting accusations from Wismichu and his ex-girlfriend Ingrid Míchel ("SoyMia"). In 2018, Dalas sued Ismael for libel and slander in the video "Así es Dalas Review", seeking nine months in jail and a 15,000 euro fine. At the end of 2019, he uploaded "Denuncié a Wismichu", discussing the lawsuit filed against Prego. On 17 December 2020, the trial on whether Wismichu slandered Dalas concluded, with the 25th criminal court of Barcelona acquitting Ismael. On 11 February 2021, Dalas claimed Ismael had a criminal record, including a 6-month prison sentence for injuring a man with a glass bottle, asserting access to his records through the lawsuit and alleging audio files of Ingrid accusing Ismael of abuse. He also accused Ismael of searching for teenagers on Chatroulette and recording them for paid, uncensored videos, and an alleged victim appeared in a video on 16 February, stating she was 14 when she showed her breasts to a friend in one of Ismael's recordings. In April 2018, a 15-year-old Argentinian girl named Olivia shared screenshots, videos, and live streams of alleged conversations with Dalas in 2016, claiming she was faking her age and that he sent her semi-nude pool photos on Instagram. This was addressed in a livestream with Mexivergas in March 2018, and in 2021, Mafian TV interviewed the alleged victim, Olivia (known as Olivita de Mar), who claimed Dalas contacted his father to intimidate him. Following these accusations, Dalas was tried on 30 November 2018 for "child sexual cyberbullying and sexual abuse", with the Madrid prosecutor's office seeking five years in prison, 11 years of disqualification, and nine years of estrangement. According to Olivia's testimony, she and Dalas began communicating via Twitter in 2015, with Dalas sending her a photo of his naked torso. They met in person on 26 January 2016 at a book signing in Madrid, and on 8 February 2016 at Atocha train station, where she claimed he kissed her, proposed going to his hotel, and later touched her vaginal area and breasts at Retiro park. Dalas denied the park visit and sexual encounter, admitted they met in person during the book signing, stated he was only at Atocha for about 15 minutes to sign a copy of the book, and denied any sexual interest in her, claiming their conversations were due to her school problems and abuse from her mother. In December 2018, the Provincial Court of Madrid acquitted Dalas. Dalas is an atheist and denies the existence of Jesus. His sister is Ariadna Cabrero Lemus, known as Ariann Music. As of 2018, he lives in Ireland with his girlfriend Damaris Pérez, known as Lizy P, a fashion and make-up YouTuber, due to high taxes in Spain. On 17 August 2022, his stepfather Manel Cabero i Pueyo (son of Manuel Cabero) died of stage 4 liver cancer with metastasis, after which Dalas criticized the health system for the treatment he received. Dalas has been controversial for political comments, occasionally supporting Republican politician Donald Trump for his economic policies and decision to designate Antifa.

As of 2018, Dalas resides in Ireland with his girlfriend Damaris Pérez, known as Lizy P, a fashion and make-up YouTuber, due to high taxes in Spain and other factors. On 17 August 2022, his stepfather Manel Cabero i Pueyo (son of Manuel Cabero) passed away from stage 4 liver cancer with metastasis, after which Dalas criticized the health system for the treatment he received. Dalas has been controversial for his political comments, including occasional support for Republican politician Donald Trump due to his economic policies and designation of Antifa as a terrorist group, as well as a video supporting the Spanish far-right party Vox for its economic policies and stance on the Spanish gender violence law, despite disliking the party’s other social positions. He has also criticized socialism, communism, progressive leftist movements in Spain, and taxes, accusing them of statism. Many of his statements have been accused of being homophobic and racist. During the 2016 Madrid Book Fair, he was expelled under feminist pressure. In a video uploaded in September 2021, he remarked, "that even if habits are changed, it is impossible for people to stop climate change, because the only people that could do something are the ones that control the industry."
